sections.heading: What Is Liquid Silicone Rubber (LSR) Molding?

blocks.text: Liquid silicone rubber molding is a specialized injection molding process used to produce flexible, durable components from two-part, heat-curable silicone materials.
Unlike conventional thermoplastic injection molding, LSR processing typically uses a cooled injection system and a heated mold.
Two liquid silicone components are precisely metered and mixed before being injected into the mold cavity. Heat activates a curing reaction that creates a permanently cross-linked elastomer.
Once curing is complete, the mold opens and the finished component is removed.
The controlled injection process enables manufacturers to produce detailed geometries, thin sections, and precision silicone components with consistent material properties.
Advantages of LSR Molding
Precision & Repeatability
Controlled material delivery, tooling, and processing support consistent production of complex molded silicone components.
Complex Geometries
LSR's flow characteristics allow it to fill detailed mold features and thin sections that may be challenging with higher-viscosity silicone materials.
High-Volume Manufacturing Potential
LSR injection molding can support efficient automated production, particularly for recurring programs with sufficient volume to justify specialized tooling.
Temperature Resistance
Silicone elastomers can maintain useful mechanical properties across a broad temperature range, depending on the selected formulation.
Environmental Durability
Silicone offers excellent resistance to weathering, ozone, ultraviolet exposure, and many aging conditions.
Material & Application Versatility
LSR is available in a variety of hardness grades and specialized formulations, including materials developed for electrical, medical, optical, and other demanding applications.
Reduced Finishing Requirements
Well-designed LSR molds and properly controlled processes can produce parts with minimal flash, reducing secondary trimming and handling.

sections.heading: Our Liquid Silicone Rubber Molding Solutions

blocks.text: SYNC supports custom silicone molding applications requiring specialized engineering, material selection, and consistent manufacturing performance.
Precision Silicone Components
LSR injection molding can produce detailed silicone components used in sealing, protection, fluid management, and mechanical assemblies.
Typical applications include:
Complex & Thin-Wall Components
LSR's relatively low viscosity during injection makes it suitable for filling intricate mold cavities.
The process is especially valuable when components require detailed sealing features, flexible walls, small geometries, or consistent part definition.
Proper tool design, gating, venting, and curing controls remain essential to achieving reliable results.
Insert Molding & Encapsulation
LSR molding can be used to encapsulate compatible inserts or create integrated assemblies combining silicone with other materials.
Applications may include electrical contacts, mechanical inserts, protective encapsulation, and specialized components.
Material compatibility, insert preparation, bonding requirements, and tooling design must be evaluated for each application.
Repeat Production & Automation
LSR injection molding can support automated material delivery, controlled injection cycles, and repeatable production.
Depending on component design and production requirements, automation can help reduce manual handling, improve consistency, and support efficient manufacturing.
Specialized Silicone Materials

LSR formulations can be selected to meet requirements involving hardness, temperature performance, mechanical strength, tear resistance, electrical properties, color, and applicable material specifications.
Our engineering teams help evaluate material options based on the intended operating environment and component requirements.
Selecting the right silicone formulation is critical to component performance.
LSR materials are commonly based on two-component, platinum-catalyzed addition-cure silicone systems. Material properties can vary substantially by grade and formulation.
Common LSR Material Options
General-Purpose LSR
Provides a balance of flexibility, mechanical properties, and temperature performance for industrial and engineered components.
Medical-Grade LSR
Specialized formulations may be selected for medical applications requiring defined material characteristics, biological evaluation, and regulatory documentation.
High-Strength LSR
Formulations designed to improve tensile or tear performance in demanding mechanical applications.
Electrical-Grade LSR
Materials selected for dielectric performance, insulation, or other specified electrical characteristics.
Specialty LSR Formulations
Additional grades may offer properties such as low compression set, optical clarity, specific hardness, or particular environmental resistance.

sections.heading: LSR Injection Molding vs. Silicone Compression Molding

blocks.text: Both processes manufacture silicone rubber components, but they differ significantly in material handling, tooling, and production economics.
Liquid Silicone Rubber Injection Molding
LSR injection molding uses liquid silicone materials delivered through controlled mixing and injection systems.
It is often well suited for intricate geometries, smaller components, consistent repeat production, and applications that benefit from automation.
Silicone Compression Molding
Compression molding typically uses high-consistency silicone rubber placed directly into a heated mold.
It can offer advantages for larger components, specialized geometries, lower production volumes, and programs where tooling flexibility is important.
Silicone Transfer Molding
Transfer molding moves uncured silicone from a separate chamber into a closed mold.
The process can be particularly useful for complex geometries, encapsulated inserts, and specialized applications requiring controlled material placement.

a.text: LSR stands for Liquid Silicone Rubber, a two-component silicone elastomer commonly processed through specialized injection molding equipment.

faq.q: What is the difference between LSR and conventional silicone rubber?

a.text: LSR is typically supplied as two liquid components and processed through controlled injection molding systems. High-consistency silicone rubber (HCR) is more commonly processed through compression, transfer, or specialized injection molding methods.
Both materials cure into silicone elastomers but require different processing approaches.

faq.q: What products can be manufactured using LSR molding?

a.text: Common examples include seals, gaskets, diaphragms, valves, flexible connectors, protective components, and precision silicone assemblies.

faq.q: Is LSR molding suitable for high-volume production?

a.text: Yes. LSR injection molding can be well suited for high-volume production, particularly where automated material delivery and repeatable cycles justify the investment in specialized tooling and equipment.

faq.q: Can LSR be used in medical applications?

a.text: Yes. Certain LSR formulations are designed for medical applications. Suitability depends on the specific material, patient-contact requirements, manufacturing controls, testing, and applicable regulatory standards.

faq.q: Can LSR components be manufactured in different hardness levels?

a.text: Yes. LSR materials are available in a range of Shore A hardness grades, with specialty formulations selected according to the application.

faq.q: Is LSR resistant to oils and chemicals?

a.text: Chemical compatibility depends on the silicone formulation, the specific chemical or fluid, temperature, and exposure duration. General-purpose LSR is not universally resistant to fuels, oils, or aggressive chemicals.

faq.q: How do I determine whether LSR or compression molding is the better option?

a.text: Part geometry, material requirements, tooling investment, production volume, and dimensional tolerances all influence process selection. SYNC can review the application and evaluate the available molding options.
